text:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a bunch of flapping in the eu-west GPU nodepool during the 11:00 spike. Autoscaler repeatedly terminates nodes while long training jobs are in Terminating for >5m :grimacing:
Priya: ugh. any eviction logs? are those pods stuck on PVs or preStop hooks?
Alex: Mostly TF jobs holding onto GPUs + PVCs. kubelet shows "deadline exceeded" when trying to evict, then CA marks node as unneeded and deletes it.
Matt: Sounds like scale-down is too aggressive. What are our flags currently? I remember we had scale-down-unneeded-time=5m to save cost.
Jing: yep, current cluster-autoscaler flags (eu-west): --scale-down-unneeded-time=5m --scale-down-unready-time=20m --max-node-provision-time=10m --expander=most-pods
Sam: two quick levers: increase unneeded time and give evictions more headroom (grace period). Also ensure pods set safe-to-evict or have PodDisruptionBudget that allows eviction.
Priya: I prototyped something: bump --scale-down-unneeded-time to 15m and set --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.45 for GPU pools. Also add --skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false (we want more conservative behavior).
Alex: can we also tune draining? some pods have long preStop cleanup (checkpointing). Maybe set --node-termination-grace-period=600s?
Matt: CA doesn't have node-termination-grace-period flag but you can control eviction pacing. We should also patch the jobs to set terminationGracePeriodSeconds and add lifecycle preStop that checkpoints faster.
Jing: proposal (safe quick patch):
```
# autoscaler flags to test on canary pool
--scale-down-unneeded-time=15m
--scale-down-unready-time=25m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
--max-node-provision-time=15m
--expander=least-waste
```
Keep expander change only on canary so we can observe packing behavior.
Sam: +1. Also add annotation to heavy-training pods: "cluster.autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict": "false" when they do checkpointing, and flip to true afterwards. Reduces churn.
Priya: note: some of the training infra uses local SSD scratch. CA will skip nodes with local storage by default, so check --skip-nodes-with-local-storage flag. If set true, we might be forcing pods to stay, and then CA treats nodes as unremovable in some cases.
Alex: good catch — current flag is --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true. For GPU pools we probably want to leave it true, but ensure jobs mark safe-to-evict during checkpoints.
Matt: operational checklist before deploying flags to prod: 1) apply to canary pool in eu-west, 2) monitor node churn metric + pending GPU pods, 3) run synthetic training job that simulates long preStop.
Jing: I'll bake a small monitoring dashboard with these panels: node-termination-count, time-to-evict, average pod.Terminating duration, pending GPU pod wait time.
Alex: Also watch for network error patterns — we saw TCP resets during eviction that made kubelet stall. Might be unrelated but correlate with CNI version and kubelet logs.
Sam: OpsBot ran a quick canary deploy earlier: "deploy autoscaler-config to eu-west-canary" succeeded. OpsBot: deployed config revision 2026-03-18_08.
Priya: After canary runs for 2 hours we should decide rollback or promote. If packing improves and churn drops, roll forward. If GPU pod wait grows, rollback.
Alex: sounds good. I'll create a short runbook for on-call: how to pause CA (scale to 0 replicas in the manager), how to revert flags, and kubectl commands for forced drain/uncordon.
Matt: snippet for ops runbook:
```
# pause autoscaler
kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment cluster-autoscaler --replicas=0
# resume
kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment cluster-autoscaler --replicas=2
# force drain (careful):
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=300
```
Jing: I'll add that to the runbook and attach links to dashboard panels.
Alex: thanks all. @Sam can you keep an eye on cost delta? longer unneeded-time will raise short-term cost. We want to quantify tradeoff.
Sam: will do. I'll post hourly updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
OpsBot: Monitoring alert suppressed for node churn while canary is active.
Priya: if we see persistent evictions >10m, we should consider adjusting job templates to checkpoint more frequently rather than prolonging scale-down forever. Long-term fix.
Alex: Agreed. For now testing flags + safe-to-evict annotation + runbook. Closing plan: canary today, monitor 2h, then decide.
Sam: update 1995550030: canary launched, no immediate increase in pending GPU pods.
Jing: update 1995550042: eviction duration dropped from median 7m -> 2m on canary nodes. Looks promising.
Alex: great, promote to eu-west main after 2h if metrics hold. :rocket:
